> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR

> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/services/service-automation/src/stored-reference-package-backfill.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **103** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 0f9b5653958e3da522d8f6490573e14997f1e4ad` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `1e8448a6eaf9f0a480c1d7443d6acbe3f0e15554` — the merge of head `6655b7421962c33d0dcaed453f01fea893c08995` into base `0f9b5653958e3da522d8f6490573e14997f1e4ad`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 1e8448a6eaf9f0a480c1d7443d6acbe3f0e15554 && git checkout 1e8448a6eaf9f0a480c1d7443d6acbe3f0e15554
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 0f9b5653958e3da522d8f6490573e14997f1e4ad 6655b7421962c33d0dcaed453f01fea893c08995 && git checkout -B drift-repro 0f9b5653958e3da522d8f6490573e14997f1e4ad && git merge --no-ff 6655b7421962c33d0dcaed453f01fea893c08995

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 0f9b5653958e3da522d8f6490573e14997f1e4ad
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 0f9b5653958e3da522d8f6490573e14997f1e4ad` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

This is a delta round after record 6781597322 (PASS on `1b655c3cd`, PR #32327). The head now carries:
- `main` with #32214;
- the exact-qualifier hunk (ruling (c));
- the CLI reads of ruling A;
- the pins for the doors `main` added.

FROM is `216674301`, the merge base and the state the PR body names. Both trees were built with `OS_SKIP_DTS=1`.

**Two must-fixes.**

**M1. The email template send door moves, undeclared and unpinned, and one moved answer serves another package's template.**
- Where: `packages/plugins/plugin-email/src/template-loader.ts:159-180` (`bundleAddressOf`). #32214 added this door.
  - It resolves the name with `resolvePackageScopedName` (line 160), then counts holders with `packageScopedHoldersOf` (line 163). Both now read the served set through the source.
  - The file is not in the diff. The PR body lists three doors `main` added (#32310, #32294, #32302) and misses this one.
- Measured with `createRegistryEmailTemplateLoader` over a real `SchemaRegistry`: once with the real protocol and once registry-only, in both registration orders. Template `welcome` is held by ALPHA (enabled) and BETA (disabled). FROM → TO:
  - send with no package (omitted or null): 409 naming both → ALPHA's template sent;
  - caller whose closure holds both: 409 naming both → ALPHA's template sent;
  - caller whose closure reaches the name only through BETA: no template → 409 `outside-closure` naming ALPHA;
  - caller that reaches neither: 409 naming both → 409 naming ALPHA;
  - both holders disabled, no package: 409 naming both → no template;
  - **caller BETA, the disabled holder itself: no template → ALPHA's template sent.**
- Why the last one is wrong:
  - The resolver answers BETA, because the caller's own holding is kept.
  - Line 163 then counts the served holders without the caller and finds one, so line 165 returns `undefined`.
  - The send reads the environment-wide list, which hides BETA. So ALPHA's template goes out for a caller that has no path to ALPHA.
  - `templateCallerPackageId` rides the delivery payload (`service-messaging/src/email-channel.ts:526`), and no disable check was found in automation or messaging. So a queued or retried delivery reaches this path.
  - Measured at the loader, not end to end.
- Pins: none. No plugin-email test disables a package at the send door. With the served filter ablated, the plugin-email file in the diff stays green.
- Fix:
  - In `bundleAddressOf`, when the resolved holder is the caller's own package and that package is disabled, read at that package's own address. That is the answer `main` gives: no template.
  - Add the six rows to the FROM → TO table and the changeset.
  - Pin them in `template-loader.test.ts`, in both orders, with a CONTROL for both enabled and for the enabled holder's own send.

**M2. Two moved answers are undeclared, and the "Not moved" line is false for them.**
- Measured through `protocol.getMetaItem` and `getMetaItems` (objectql harness, real registry). Dashboard `dup` is held by A (disabled) and B (enabled), plus a package-less row (the environment's item, or a `sys_metadata` row with no package).
  - `?package=A` and `?package=A.custom`: 409 `ambiguous-in-closure` naming both → 404 (A's withheld item). The body and changeset say these addresses "keep their 404", but with a package-less row `main` answered 409.
  - The list scoped to B: B's own item → the package-less row as B's customization. The body and changeset say the served lists do not move.
- Both follow from row 26 and are the right answers. They are not declared and not pinned.
- Fix: add both rows, correct the "Not moved" line, and pin each, one pin per door.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Carry-forward is clean.**
  - The four files of the last merge are byte-identical on `main` (`216674301`) and on #32214's branch (`27abd458a`).
  - Against PR #32327's own patches, only four files' source hunks differ: `protocol-exact-qualifier.ts` (new), `protocol-meta-item-face.ts`, `stored-package-references.ts`, and the docblock in `connector-package-scope.ts`. Every other source hunk is unchanged since the r3 PASS.
- **Touched suites.** All 22 test files of the diff pass on this head: 975 tests across 11 packages.
- **Ablation A1, the served filter in `packageScopedHoldersOf`.**
  - 245 of 975 red: rest 81, runtime 85, objectql 73, service-automation 3, plugin-security 1, plugin-approvals 1.
  - The durable pins (core, sharing, email, cli) stay green, as they should.
- **Ablation A2, `disabledExactAddressHolder` returns nothing.** rest 15 red, runtime 15 red, objectql 2 red. This matches the dev's 15 of 30 per transport.
- **Ablation A3, `includeDisabledPackages` ignored.** Every durable family goes red: sharing 1, plugin-security 1, service-automation 4, plugin-approvals 1, plugin-email 1, cli 4, objectql 6, rest 64, runtime 64.
- **Security catalog guards.**
  - Dropping `heldInAnyPackage` from `holdsPlatformPermissionSet` turns 2 of 39 red.
  - Dropping the two catalog not-found guards turns 5 of 39 red.
- **Rows 23 to 26, measured FROM and TO.**
  - Row 23 holds. The pair of a disabled base, with an enabled holder registered first, moves from the disabled body under the enabled envelope to a withheld item. The execution face and the draft read withhold it too.
  - Rows 24 and 25 hold through their pins.
  - Row 26 holds at the enabled holder's exact address.
- **Rows 1 to 22.** Their code is unchanged since r3. Their pins are green and go red under ablation.
- **Class sweep of every `packageScopedHoldersOf` and `resolvePackageScopedName` caller.**
  - Doors on the served set:
    - the registry readers, the resolver and the action wrapper;
    - `automation-address.ts`;
    - the exact qualifier's candidates and pair bases, the caller arm and the namespace path;
    - the connector and flow execute doors;
    - the webhook and sharing readers.
  - Durable reads on every holder:
    - the R1/R3, R4, R5/R6/R13, R7 to R11 and R20 backfills;
    - the CLI report (`ask`, `pairMembers`, `packageLessRows`);
    - `picklistReferenceVerdict`.
  - One door does neither correctly: the email send door (M1). It is on the served set, but it mixes a caller-aware resolution with a caller-blind holder count.
- **CI on this head.** 70 check runs: 57 success, 13 skipped, 0 failed, 0 pending.
- **Trial merges (not pushed).**
  - `origin/main` 67c49d778: clean. One shared file, `packages/metadata/src/metadata-manager.ts`.
  - `origin/claude/project-thread-wqgmuu` (#32507): clean. Four shared files.
  - `origin/claude/project-thread-du44hj` (#32513): conflicts in one file, `packages/runtime/src/domains/meta-qualified-item-read.test.ts`, in two hunks (the import block, and a `describe` both sides add).

### ② Semver level

- `patch` on twelve packages with the BREAKING banner is right for what is declared. Both declaration lines are in the body and the changeset.
- The changeset is incomplete by M1 and M2.
- plugin-email is already listed, so the fix adds lines, not a package, unless it touches `service-messaging`.
- Row 23 is correctly declared as a narrowing at a door.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **#32513 after both land.**
  - Its new `judgePicklistArrival` (objectql `registry.ts`) calls `resolvePackageScopedName` for `picklist` with no `includeDisabledPackages`.
  - This PR makes the picklist verdict a durable read.
  - Whichever lands second must add the option there, or the install audit and the field verdict will disagree for a disabled holder.
- **#32507 lands first.**
  - The merge is textually clean.
  - The flow doors it adds will judge the served set through the source, as rows 10 to 12 did.
  - That head owes a delta read and rows for those doors.
- **Unmoved and already filed.** Each answers the same on both trees.
  - `?package=B.custom` of an enabled B answers 404 when a disabled holder registered first (#32501, location 1).
  - An App's pair with one module disabled answers 404 when the disabled module registered first and no outside package holds the name. Row 24's 200 holds only with an outside holder registered first, as the row says (#32501, location 2).
  - A disabled package's item that exists only as a stored row is served at `?package=DISABLED` under another holder's envelope (#32354).
- **Read-then-save of a mixed name** is carded on #32354, with an epic ruling (6781691009). It is not in this diff.
- **Not run:** the full package suites (only the touched files), typecheck, lint, the dogfood battery, and the email send through the HTTP doors.

### ④ Design judgment

- The narrowing itself holds against the published contract.
  - A disabled package's body is served nowhere on the reads this diff touches.
  - The exact address of a disabled package, or of a pair whose every base is disabled, answers that package's withheld item, whatever envelope a layer reached.
  - Admission reads every holder, and candidates name served holders only.
- Break attempts on the new hunk that held:
  - a disabled base with a pair override row;
  - a disabled base beside an enabled holder, in both orders, on plain, execution and draft reads;
  - a non-holder address of an only-disabled name;
  - the environment's item and a package-less stored row beside a mixed name;
  - a stored row bound to the disabled holder.
- The break attempt that did not hold is M1: the new source rule "the caller's own holding stays" meets a door that counts holders without the caller.
- Should-fix: the scoped-list reader `pairMemberWithheldAt` (`protocol-exact-qualifier.ts:622`) also judges served holders now.
  - An App pair's undeclared row, with one module disabled, should get a row and a pin beside the M2 list row.
  - Read, not measured.
- Nits, unchanged from r3:
  - the mixed-name rule lives in three places;
  - `disabledOnlyHolderOf` and the every-base-disabled arm pick the first disabled holder;
  - the `outside-closure` arm of `withholdDisabledHolder` is unreachable.
- Size: 2536 lines, about 1900 of them tests. It should not have been split.
  - Ruling (c) tied the qualifier hunk to this card.
  - The doors `main` adds must be declared where the source moves.
  - The M1 fix belongs here too, because this change creates the wrong answer.
